scope: Replace unverifiable Gordić illustrations in inference physics and benchmarking, preserving all original source-library content and direct source links.

review.source: Harvard ML Systems vol. II, Performance Engineering: original prefill/decode roofline; vol. III, §2.8.1 and Figure 5: initial logits, first sample, client delivery, and buffered remaining tokens. Stanford CS336 Lecture 10: nominal dense-BF16 H100 SXM ceiling and bandwidth. Original Gordić article retained as a linked alternative and unchanged source-library page.
review.worked_cases: H100 roofline at 128, 256 and 512 FLOP/byte gives upper bounds of 428.8, 857.6 and 989 TFLOP/s. Two four-token streams both have TTFT 200 ms, last-token E2E 380 ms, and an endpoint-normalized 60 ms/token. Observed gaps are 60/60/60 ms versus 180 ms; the second stream does not identify individual token emission times.
review.figure_choice: The candidate SGLang/Datawhale course Figure 5.4 was not used: the drawing divides elapsed time after the first token by total N, while the chapter example uses N-1, and the timeline misaligns the first-token labels. Harvard's byte-identical figure distinguishes service and client and leaves the benchmark convention to the text.
review.preservation: Inside vLLM.md SHA-256 remains 9662caac4b2f93ca1ea095bf473982c94dda7ab499222d4688838a03f34b070c. Old PNGs and their source links remain in the library; the two figures still have no verified republication grant there. Original JAX Appendix A and the benchmark source excerpts and code stay unchanged. No publication.
review.style: Read both input chapters in each locale and reread the revised passages. The new prose follows actual chart labels, keeps source artwork unchanged, and distinguishes engine work, client-visible events and normalized averages.
review.verification: Final local build: 2083 pages, zero broken internal links, 300 output tests. All 26 displayed CPU code blocks in the two editions and five hash-pinned reversals passed. Registry and public-assets suites checked; after adding the required curated ML systems manifest entry, its one initially failing coverage test passed. Both figures were inspected at 1280 and 375 px; the first-token SVG zooms and pans at 3× on mobile. The 310-page reader scan found 1214 SHA-matching figure paths and five rights flags.

*Arithmetic and memory-bandwidth ceilings. Implementations may operate below either ceiling. changes.new:
On the sloping part of the curve, doubling $I$ doubles the bound:
128 FLOP/byte gives $128\cdot3.35=428.8$ TFLOP/s, and 256 FLOP/byte
gives $857.6$ TFLOP/s. At 512 FLOP/byte, $I W_{\max}$ already exceeds
989 TFLOP/s, so the flat arithmetic ceiling sets the bound. These are
H100 calculations, not values read from the schematic Harvard plot.
A real kernel can fall below the bound at the same intensity.
The [plot in Inside vLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm-project.github.io/05f81b0527e2d484c48721f9dc1c49d06849c9f3/assets/figures/2025-vllm-anatomy/roofline.png)

On the upper track, `Prompt prefill` ends with the initial logits.

bracket starts before queueing and ends only when the client receives
`Token 1`. Ordinary decoding needs $K-1$ passes to produce the remaining
$K-1$ tokens. They arrive in one buffered chunk on the lower track,
so the client sees when the chunk arrived, but not the timing of

Верхняя дорожка относится к серверу, нижняя — к клиенту.
Между `Send` и `Token 1` проходят очередь, prefill, выбор токена
и его доставка. Скобка `Server prefill` охватывает только вычисление
до начальных логитов. Остальные токены на рисунке приходят одним
событием: для них нет отдельных клиентских меток. [Шкала из статьи Inside vLLM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm-project.github.io/05f81b0527e2d484c48721f9dc1c49d06849c9f3/assets/figures/2025-vllm-anatomy/latency_diagram.png) показывает, где на клиенте начинаются и заканчиваются TTFT, ITL и E2E ([статья](https://www.aleksagordic.com/blog/vllm)).

changes.old: ### Событие потока и токен не всегда совпадают
changes.new: ### Событие потока и токен не всегда совпадают

changes.old: токенов. Сетевой пакет, SSE-событие и токен модели являются разными единицами.
changes.new:
токенов. Сетевой пакет, SSE-событие и токен модели являются разными единицами.

Сравним два потока по четыре токена. Во втором первый токен
приходит отдельно, как на рисунке, а остальные три — вместе.

| Токенов в событии | Метки клиента, мс | Паузы между событиями, мс |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1, 1, 1, 1 | 200, 260, 320, 380 | 60, 60, 60 |
| 1, 3 | 200, 380 | 180 |

У обоих потоков TTFT равен 200 мс, E2E — 380 мс, а среднее
на токен по двум крайним меткам составляет $(380-200)/(4-1)=60$ мс.
По нему нельзя отличить ровную выдачу от паузы в 180 мс. Во втором
случае клиент не знает, когда сервер сгенерировал три токена, и по
одному событию не может определить, почему их доставили вместе.

changes.old: ### Stream events are not necessarily individual tokens
changes.new: ### Stream events are not necessarily individual tokens

changes.old:
different units.

Suppose six tokens arrive in three two-token chunks at 200, 300, and 500 ms.
changes.new:
different units.

Compare two streams of four tokens. In the second, the first token
arrives on its own and the next three arrive together, as in the figure.

| Tokens per event | Client timestamps, ms | Gaps between events, ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1, 1, 1, 1 | 200, 260, 320, 380 | 60, 60, 60 |
| 1, 3 | 200, 380 | 180 |

Both have a TTFT of 200 ms and an E2E of 380 ms. The token-normalized
mean from the endpoints is $(380-200)/(4-1)=60$ ms in both cases.
That number cannot distinguish the steady stream from the 180-ms
pause. The client cannot tell when the server generated each of the
three later tokens or why they arrived in one event.
